stem: Which of the following describes the typical natural history of cow's milk allergy in children?

options.text: Approximately $90\%$ of children grow out of the allergy by three years of age.
Most children will continue to have the allergy until adolescence.
Only about $10\%$ of children will ever achieve full tolerance to cow's milk.
Resolution usually occurs only if the child avoids even baked forms of milk.

explanation: The source states that while $60\%$ resolve by 12 months, the resolution rate climbs to $90\%$ by age three.
rationale: Look for a high percentage of resolution that occurs within the first few years of life.

optionExplanations.A: The source states that while $60\%$ resolve by 12 months, the resolution rate climbs to $90\%$ by age three.
optionExplanations.B: Milk and egg allergies have a high propensity for being outgrown early in childhood unlike nut or seafood allergies.
optionExplanations.C: This describes the persistence of allergies like peanut or tree nut, not milk or egg.
optionExplanations.D: The food ladder approach suggests that consuming baked milk can actually be a pragmatic part of the journey toward tolerance.
